meta.title: Media & Press
meta.description: Press contact, key facts and brand assets for journalists covering SafeSiso — an AI-powered WhatsApp service for adolescent girls in Northern Ghana.

hero.title: For journalists
hero.intro: Everything here is on the record and free to use. If you need something that isn't on this page, please get in touch rather than inferring it.

contact.heading: Press contact
contact.body: For interviews, comment, or anything not covered here.
contact.responseNote: SafeSiso is a small pilot team, so please allow a little time for a reply.

facts.heading: Key facts
facts.intro: Accurate as of this page's last update. Please use these rather than paraphrasing from elsewhere.

items.label: What it is
items.value: An AI-powered WhatsApp chatbot giving adolescent girls confidential, shame-free access to sexual and reproductive health information, with automated risk detection and referral to verified safe spaces.

items.label: Who it serves
items.value: Girls aged 10 to 18 in rural and peri-urban communities across the Northern, Upper East and Upper West regions of Ghana.

items.label: Origin
items.value: The winning innovation at the AI4HerFuture Hackathon, organised by UNFPA Ghana and the Africa Health Innovation Centre (AHIC).

items.label: Funding
items.value: The AI for Her Future Innovation Hackathon Seed Fund, supported by UNFPA Ghana and the Government of Canada.

items.label: Delivery partner
items.value: The Planned Parenthood Association of Ghana (PPAG).

items.label: The referral network
items.value: SafeHer — a verified, live directory of local safe spaces that reflects real availability, so a girl is never referred somewhere that cannot receive her.

items.label: Current status
items.value: Pilot stage, pre-launch. No usage figures exist yet; the Impact page will carry live, anonymized figures once the service is running.

reporting.heading: Reporting on SafeSiso responsibly
reporting.intro: We ask this of every journalist covering the programme, and it is not negotiable for us.

points.title: We cannot introduce you to a girl who has used SafeSiso
points.body: Not because we would rather not — because we cannot. The service never collects a name, an age or a location, so there is no way to identify a single user. That is the whole design, and a request for case studies cannot be met without breaking it.

points.title: Please do not seek out individual users
points.body: Approaching girls in target communities to ask whether they have used SafeSiso puts them at risk of exactly the exposure the service exists to prevent.

points.title: Please do not publish safe space addresses
points.body: SafeHer partner locations are published by region only. Naming an exact address in coverage could expose both the organization and the girls seen entering it.

points.title: SafeSiso is not an emergency service
points.body: If your coverage may reach girls at risk, please make that clear and point readers to emergency services and trusted local support alongside SafeSiso.

assets.heading: Brand assets
assets.body: Logo files, usage guidance and approved colour references for use in coverage.
assets.logoBody: The shield mark shown here is the official SafeSiso logo, used alongside the SafeSiso wordmark. Please reproduce them together where space allows.

assets.colourNote: WhatsApp green is used on this site only for the button that starts a chat. It is not a SafeSiso brand colour.
